item.title: FYI: News Briefs in HVAC - February 16, 2026
item.description: For your information news briefs from a wide variety of categories within the HVAC industry. Price increases, mergers and acquisitions, award winners, and more are highlighted here each issue.

item.title: Electrification Laws Gain Momentum, Forcing HVAC Contractors to Adapt
item.description: From equipment restrictions to incentive-driven transitions, state electrification efforts are influencing how contractors sell, install, and plan for the future.

item.title: Airborne Act Reintroduced
item.description: Two House members, a Democrat and a Republican, revived a bill that was also considered in previous sessions.

item.title: Know a Champion of Distribution? Tell us!
item.description: A new awards program, Champions of Distribution, highlights the people and companies making a difference in distribution.

item.title: HVAC Trends: Artificial Intelligence and HVACR
item.description: Jimmy Thompson, senior sales manager, HVAC, at Podium, talked with us about how AI helps contractors communicate with homeowners, how contractors can take the first step toward implementing AI, how AI can help build authentic connections, and the biggest AI barrier’s he’s seeing from techs in the field.

item.title: How Machine Learning Is Transforming Demand Forecasting for HVAC Distributors
item.description: The partners in Lantern, a machine learning software firm focused on product distribution, pitched the technology to HVACR distributors during the recent HARDI conference.

item.title: ABB Introduces New UL Type 12 and Type 4X Vertical Bypass Drives
item.description: ACH580 drives deliver motor control, energy efficiency, and intuitive operation for a wide range of HVACR equipment, including fans, pumps, and compressors.

item.title: How to Increase Close Rates
item.description: More options, financing, bundled warranties, and payment-first pricing aren’t upsells — they’re the path to better close rates and bigger tickets.

item.title: Smardt AIR Enters North American HVAC Market
item.description: The new company is now setting up its customer service, engineering, and internal sales department to begin shipping custom and semi-custom commercial air handling products in the third quarter of 2026 from its newly acquired Phoenix, Arizona headquarters.

item.title: Solving the HVAC Contractor Shortage: How to Increase Licensing Accessibility
item.description: Thousands of techs are ready to advance. Licensing bottlenecks are what’s holding the industry back.
